items.text: Run a VIN history check (e.g. carVertical) for mileage and accident history.
Ask for the VIN and a photo of the registration certificate before travelling.
Arrange to see the car in daylight, with the engine cold.
Registration certificate in the seller’s name.
A valid technical inspection (TA).
Service book or invoices showing regular oil changes.
How many owners the car has had.
Why they are selling.
Start the engine from cold: it should start easily, with no smoke or loud rattles.
After starting, all dashboard warning lights go out within a few seconds.
Check for rust on the sills, wheel arches and under the doors.
Look for uneven panel gaps or paint that doesn’t match (signs of accident repair).
Tyres: same brand per axle, even wear, at least 3 mm of tread.
Gears change smoothly, with no crunching, jerks or slipping.
Brakes stop straight, without vibration.
Steering stays straight on a flat road; no knocks over bumps.
No unusual knocks, whines or rattles at any speed.
Air conditioning blows cold.
The seller wants a deposit before you have seen the car.
The seller won’t share the VIN.
The car isn’t at the seller’s address.
The price is far below every similar ad.
You’re pushed to decide today.
